From: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@orbitanalytics.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing exhibit feedback & question on surcharge smoothing

Karthik —

Thanks for sending the draft pricing exhibit. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed and returned a few redlines (attached). Two high-level asks before we go to legal markups:

1) Can you confirm how Redwood defines the “surcharge smoothing” trigger? The draft references a monthly smoothing surcharge if usage variance > 40% but doesn’t include the calculation example or a lookback window. Procurement needs a clear formula.

2) The anchor/concession matrix in Exhibit B ties discounts to committed tiers but doesn’t explain how temporary capacity bursts are treated — are they counted toward the tier for discounting or billed separately?

3) Order form currently has a floor clause that reads as a hard annual minimum; our CFO wants a mutual true-up mechanism (annual true-up + pro rata in case of termination).

We’ve attached a redlined PDF (Orbit_Pricing_Exhibit_v2.pdf) with inline legal comments. Can your team propose language for: (a) smoothing trigger + example calculation, (b) a concession matrix definition that excludes ephemeral bursts, and (c) a termination true-up flow?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Orbit’s procurement cycle is tight and we’d like to get to a signable exhibit in the next week if possible.

Best,
Sara Mitchell
Head of Procurement
Orbit Analytics

Sara —

Thanks for the redlines and clear asks. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Marissa (Revenue/CS ops) to propose concrete drafting and an anchor/concession definition.

Preliminary notes from my side:
- We can provide a worked example for the smoothing surcharge (monthly vs rolling 30-day lookback) — we prefer rolling 30-day to avoid month-boundary artifacts.
- Ephemeral bursts (auto-scale spikes under 72 hours) are typically billed outside committed volumes; we can clarify that in the concession matrix and add an explicit carve-out.
- For termination true-up, Redwood supports an annual true-up; we can propose mutual pro rata offsets and a 60-day cure window.

I’m attaching a short comment doc with initial thoughts (karthik_initial_comments.docx). Laura/Marissa — can you advise on the precise legal language we should offer and whether any of these concessions require revenue-recognition or billing system changes?

Thanks — I’ll hold Orbit’s timeline in mind (they’d like sign-off next week).

Karthik —

Quick internal legal run-through and suggested redline bullets below (for Marissa to weigh in on ops/billing implications). Paste these into a tracked-changes order form and we’ll send to Orbit as our counter.

1) Surcharge smoothing: define as follows — "Smoothing surcharge applies when the 30-day rolling average of billed tokens for a given billing SKU decreases below 60% of the committed monthly tier for any continuous 30-day window. Smoothing surcharge = (Committed tier daily rate - Actual 30-day rolling average daily rate) * days in billing period; example calculations provided in Appendix A."
- Rationale: rolling window avoids month-end distortions.

2) Ephemeral bursts carve-out: "Transient bursts are defined as individual autoscale events lasting <= 72 hours and capped at 2 events per calendar month. Transient bursts shall be excluded from committed-tier calculations for the purposes of discount eligibility (but will be billed at on-demand rates)."
- Rationale: protects Orbit from losing discount credit for short-term scaling tests.

3) True-up / termination flow: "Annual true-up: Parties will reconcile committed vs actual usage on an annual basis. If actual usage < committed, Customer will be invoiced for the shortage pro rata; if actual usage > committed, Customer shall receive credit toward future invoices. On termination, the parties shall perform a final true-up for the then-current annual period and any unpaid shortage shall be due within 45 days unless parties agree to an alternative payment schedule."
- Note: propose 45 days to balance collections vs commercial flexibility.

4) Concession matrix clarity: Add explicit definitions for "Committed volume, Burst volume, and Baseline smoothing" and a mapping table (Appendix B) that ties % discount to net committed ARR bands. Insert a clause that discounts are adjusted only at annual renewal unless both parties agree otherwise.

Marissa: operational questions — can billing support the 30-day rolling metric and the burst exclusion rules? Also: any impact to revenue deferral if we add a true-up liability? If ops cannot support the rolling calculation, we may have to fall back to calendar-month calculations.

If Orbital legal counters on the 72-hour / 2-events cap, I recommend a middle-ground: 5 events per quarter or a separate lab/test allowance.

— Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Sara —

Appreciate the clear comments and timeline. Please find attached our redlined order form (redlined_orderform_20261215.xlsx) and a short summary of the changes below. We believe this set addresses Orbit’s asks while keeping the billing surface stable.

Summary of material changes (high level):
- Smoothing surcharge: defined as a 30-day rolling calculation with worked example in Appendix A; surcharge only applies where rolling average falls below 60% of committed daily rate for a continuous 30-day window.
- Burst carve-out: transient bursts <= 72 hours and <= 2 events/month excluded from discount tier calculations; billed at published on-demand rates.
- Annual true-up & termination: annual reconciliation required; final termination true-up payable within 45 days. Credits for over-usage applied to next invoice within the following billing cycle.
- Anchor/concession matrix: clarified that discounts are tied to net committed ARR (excluding burst volume) and that discount bands may be re-evaluated only at renewal unless otherwise agreed.

Attachments: redlined_orderform_20261215.xlsx (tracked changes) and Appendix A (worked calculation examples).
